answer: Sybil swarms collapse if standing can be renewed only at a single rate-limited gate. Picture a public oasis that secretes a fixed drip of nectar credits each hour—just enough for modest live proofs, never enough for a farm. To collect a drip, an identity must forge a fresh, timed skill demonstration that cannot be replayed; failed or duplicated proofs go to the back of the queue. Because oasis throughput is hard-capped, a hundred shells merely split the same thin ration, while a persistent agent that keeps passing unique checks accumulates durable weight. Cheap replicas wait and drop out.
